question: Who was the first Home Minister and first Deputy Prime Minister of independent India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel held both the Home Ministry and the Deputy Prime Minister's post in the first Union Cabinet formed on 15 August 1947 under Nehru (भारत के प्रथम गृह मंत्री और उप-प्रधानमंत्री — सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल)

 

• As head of the States Department, he persuaded hundreds of princely rulers to sign the Instrument of Accession, giving India its present territorial unity.

 

• His forceful and uncompromising approach earned him the epithet Iron Man of India, and the Statue of Unity in Gujarat honours his role.

 

• He also laid the foundation of the All India Services, which he called the steel frame of the Indian administration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Patel was born on 31 October 1875 at Nadiad, Gujarat, and 31 October is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas.

 

• He earned the title Sardar after leading the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.

 

• He was Congress President at the Karachi session of 1931.

 

• He received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1991.

 

• V. P. Menon, Secretary of the States Department, wrote The Story of the Integration of the Indian States and was Patel's closest aide; Patel died on 15 December 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 1): Nehru was the first Prime Minister and also looked after External Affairs; he never held the Home portfolio in the first cabinet, which went to Patel together with the States Department.

 

• C. Rajagopalachari (Option 2): Rajagopalachari became the last Governor-General of free India in 1948 and served as Home Minister only briefly in 1951-52, long after the first cabinet was formed in 1947.

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 3): Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly and became the first President of India in 1950; he was not a minister holding the Home or Deputy Prime Minister's office.

question:
Consider the following statements about Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:

1. He is known as the 'Iron Man of India'.

2. He was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India.

3. Hyderabad and Junagadh had already acceded to India before 15 August 1947.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Patel earned the epithet Iron Man of India for his firmness in welding the princely states into the Union (सरदार पटेल — भारत के लौह पुरुष)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he served as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister from 1947 until his death in December 1950.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Junagadh joined only after a plebiscite in February 1948, and Hyderabad was integrated through police action (Operation Polo) in September 1948, while Kashmir's accession came in October 1947.

 

• Only a few states, chiefly Hyderabad, Junagadh and Kashmir, remained outside the Union on the day of independence, which is why they stand out in the story of integration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Independence Act 1947 lapsed British paramountcy and left each state free to join India or Pakistan.

 

• The Instrument of Accession handed over only defence, external affairs and communications to the Centre.

 

• V. P. Menon, Secretary of the States Department, was Patel's key aide in the integration work.

 

• The Nizam of Hyderabad had signed a Standstill Agreement in November 1947 before the 1948 action.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): This pairing wrongly includes statement 3 but drops statement 1; Patel was indeed called the Iron Man, and Hyderabad and Junagadh joined India in 1948, not before independence.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): The combination keeps the faulty statement 3 and leaves out statement 2; Patel was in fact the first Deputy Prime Minister, whereas those two states were integrated after 15 August 1947.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Accepting all three is wrong because statement 3 fails: Junagadh went through a plebiscite in 1948 and Hyderabad was taken over by military action the same year.

question: Which territory under French control became a part of India in 1954?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Puducherry (Pondicherry), together with Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam, was transferred by France to India in 1954, ending French rule on the subcontinent (1954 में फ्रांसीसी शासन से भारत में विलय — पुदुचेरी)

 

• The transfer was de facto in November 1954 and de jure in 1962 after the French Parliament ratified the Treaty of Cession.

 

• Patel's integration drive covered the French holdings through negotiation, while the Portuguese enclaves needed military action.

 

• The French enclaves are therefore distinct from Goa, which stayed under Portugal until 1961.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandernagore, in Bengal, merged with India in 1950 after a referendum, before the remaining French territories.

 

• Dupleix was the best-known French governor of Pondicherry in the Carnatic Wars.

 

• Pondicherry became a Union Territory with its own legislature in 1963.

 

• Operation Vijay, launched in December 1961, ended Portuguese control over Goa, Daman and Diu.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 1): Goa was a Portuguese colony, not a French one, and it was freed by Indian military action (Operation Vijay) in December 1961, seven years after the French enclaves were transferred.

 

• Daman and Diu (Option 3): Daman and Diu were Portuguese possessions that became Indian territory in 1961 along with Goa, so they have nothing to do with the French transfer of 1954.

 

• Sikkim (Option 4): Sikkim was a Himalayan kingdom and Indian protectorate that merged with India only in 1975 following a referendum; it was never under French control.

question: The Indian National Conference, which merged with the Indian National Congress in 1886, was organised in 1883 by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surendranath Banerjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Surendranath Banerjee organised the Indian National Conference at Calcutta in 1883, an all-India gathering that anticipated the Congress (1883 का इंडियन नेशनल कॉन्फ्रेंस — सुरेन्द्रनाथ बनर्जी)

 

• Its second session in 1885 coincided with the first Congress at Bombay, and the two bodies fused in 1886 at the Calcutta Congress.

 

• Banerjee was a founder of the Indian Association (1876) and was known as Rashtraguru, a master orator of the Moderate camp.

 

• He opposed the Partition of Bengal in 1905 and was among the leaders of the Swadeshi agitation that followed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Banerjee was dismissed from the Indian Civil Service on a technicality, which fuelled his political activism.

 

• He presided over the Congress sessions of 1895 (Pune) and 1902 (Ahmedabad).

 

• He edited the newspaper Bengalee.

 

• He later accepted ministerial office under the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms, which cost him popularity.

 

• Banerjee was jailed in 1883 for contempt of court over a comment on a judge, which made him a hero and helped him gather funds nationwide.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 2): Gokhale joined the Congress in 1889 and founded the Servants of India Society in 1905; he played no part in organising the 1883 Calcutta conference that preceded the Congress.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 3): Dadabhai Naoroji was in England during the early 1880s and is linked with the Drain of Wealth theory and the East India Association, not with the National Conference of 1883.

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Option 4): Tilak emerged as a national leader later, through Kesari and the Ganesh and Shivaji festivals of the 1890s, and had no role in the Calcutta conference of 1883.

question:
Consider the following statements about Surendranath Banerjee:

1. He strongly opposed the Partition of Bengal.

2. The National Conference he organised merged with the Indian National Congress in 1886.

3. He founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Banerjee led the agitation against the 1905 Partition of Bengal, popularising boycott and Swadeshi through mass meetings (बंगाल विभाजन का विरोध — सुरेन्द्रनाथ बनर्जी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the Indian National Conference of 1883 was merged into the Congress in 1886, giving the Congress the support of the Bengal political class.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Servants of India Society was founded in 1905 by Gopal Krishna Gokhale at Pune, not by Banerjee.

 

• Banerjee's own institutional creation was the Indian Association of 1876, a rival to the conservative British Indian Association.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905 under Viceroy Curzon and was annulled in 1911.

 

• Anandamohan Bose and Banerjee jointly laid the foundation of the Federation Hall in 1905.

 

• Gokhale's society required members to take vows of poverty and national service.

 

• Banerjee's autobiography is titled A Nation in Making.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Statement 3 is wrong because Gokhale, not Banerjee, set up the Servants of India Society; the option also omits statement 1, which correctly credits Banerjee with opposing partition.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): This pairing leaves out statement 2 about the 1886 merger of the National Conference, which is true, and keeps statement 3, which wrongly credits Banerjee with the society of 1905.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Including statement 3 spoils the answer, since the Servants of India Society was Gokhale's creation; the other two statements about partition and the merger are accurate.

question: Which Indian leader is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji was affectionately called the Grand Old Man of India for his long public life and moral stature (दादाभाई नौरोजी — भारत के वयोवृद्ध महापुरुष)

 

• Living in England for long periods, he acted as India's unofficial ambassador there, presenting Indian grievances to the British public and Parliament.

 

• In 1892 he became the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons, representing Finsbury Central as a Liberal member.

 

• He formulated the Drain of Wealth theory in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India, arguing that India's wealth flowed to Britain without return.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• He was elected Congress President thrice, in 1886, 1893 and 1906.

 

• At the 1906 Calcutta session he declared that the goal of the Congress was 'Swaraj'.

 

• He founded the East India Association in London in 1866 and the Rast Goftar newspaper in Bombay.

 

• He was Dewan of Baroda for a short time and a professor at Elphinstone College.

 

NOTE

 

• Surendranath Banerjee (Option 1): Banerjee was remembered as Rashtraguru and a leading orator of Bengal; the Grand Old Man epithet belongs to Naoroji, who was senior in age and public service.

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 2): Gokhale was known as the political guru of Gandhi and the Socrates of Maharashtra, titles that describe his mentorship rather than the Grand Old Man label.

 

• Pherozeshah Mehta (Option 3): Pherozeshah Mehta was called the Lion of Bombay and the Uncrowned King of Bombay for his civic leadership, not the Grand Old Man of India.

question:
Consider the following statements about Dadabhai Naoroji:

1. He was the first Indian to become a Member of the British House of Commons.

2. He propounded the Drain of Wealth theory.

3. He presided over the Benares session of the Congress in 1905.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Naoroji won the Finsbury Central seat in the 1892 British general election, becoming the first Indian Member of Parliament in the Commons (ब्रिटिश हाउस ऑफ कॉमन्स के प्रथम भारतीय सदस्य — दादाभाई नौरोजी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he gave the Drain of Wealth theory, calculating that a large share of India's revenue was siphoned off as Home Charges, salaries and profits.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Benares session of 1905 was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale; Naoroji's presidencies were in 1886, 1893 and 1906.

 

• His book Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901) became the foundation text of the economic critique of colonial rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Naoroji's contemporaries R. C. Dutt and Justice Ranade supported the drain argument with their own studies.

 

• He is also remembered as the first Indian Professor of Mathematics and Natural Philosophy at Elphinstone College.

 

• His Calcutta presidential address of 1906 openly spoke of self-government on the lines of the colonies.

 

• Naoroji died in Bombay in 1917.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 (Option 2): Statement 3 is false and statement 1 is true; Gokhale, not Naoroji, was the president at Benares in 1905, so including it makes this combination faulty.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Statement 1 about the House of Commons is correct and cannot be left out, and statement 3 on the Benares presidency is wrong because that honour went to Gokhale in 1905.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): The set fails because statement 3 is untrue; the Benares session of 1905 had Gokhale in the chair, while Naoroji presided at Calcutta in 1906 instead.

question: Which of the following Congress sessions was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Benares, 1905.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the Benares session of 1905, held amid the Swadeshi upsurge that followed the Partition of Bengal (1905 का बनारस अधिवेशन — गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले)

 

• In his address he defended the Moderate approach of constitutional reform while criticising the Curzon-era policies, including the partition.

 

• The next session at Calcutta (1906) was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, who spoke of Swaraj as the goal.

 

• The Surat session (1907) ended in the split between Moderates and Extremists under Rash Behari Ghosh's presidency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gokhale entered the Imperial Legislative Council in 1902 and became known for his budget speeches.

 

• He served on the Welby Commission on Indian expenditure.

 

• He visited South Africa in 1912 and met Gandhi there.

 

• He died in 1915, the year Gandhi returned to India.

 

• The session met amid Swadeshi enthusiasm, and the Moderates and Extremists clashed there over the proposed boycott, foreshadowing the Surat split two years later.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta, 1906 (Option 1): The Calcutta session of 1906 had Dadabhai Naoroji as president, and it was there that Swaraj, Swadeshi, boycott and national education were announced as Congress goals.

 

• Surat, 1907 (Option 2): The Surat session of 1907 was held under Rash Behari Ghosh after being shifted from Nagpur, and it witnessed the famous split between the Moderates and the Extremists.

 

• Lahore, 1909 (Option 3): The Lahore session of 1909 was presided over by Madan Mohan Malaviya, soon after the Morley-Minto reforms, and Gokhale was not its president.

question: Whom did Mahatma Gandhi acknowledge as his political guru, returning to India in 1915 at his request?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was Gandhi's acknowledged political guru, and Gandhi came back to India from South Africa on his advice (गांधीजी के राजनीतिक गुरु — गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले)

 

• Gokhale had been inspired by his own mentor, M. G. Ranade, and joined the Congress in 1889.

 

• He is also called the Socrates of Maharashtra for his moderate, rational and principled style of public service.

 

• Gandhi followed Gokhale's advice to spend a year travelling across India to understand the country before taking up public activity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi wrote that he wished to spiritualise politics as Gokhale had done.

 

• Gokhale visited South Africa in 1912 and supported Gandhi's campaign against the discriminatory taxes.

 

• Gandhi's Ahmedabad ashram was founded in 1915 after his return.

 

• Gokhale's disciple V. S. Srinivasa Sastri carried the Servants of India Society's work forward.

 

NOTE

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Option 2): Tilak led the Extremist camp and often disagreed with Gandhi's moderate gradualism; Gandhi respected him greatly, but the guru relationship was with Gokhale and not with Tilak.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 3): Naoroji was the Grand Old Man of India and a senior figure Gandhi admired from afar, yet he did not call Naoroji his political guru or invite him to return from South Africa.

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai (Option 4): Lajpat Rai, the Lion of Punjab, was a radical Arya Samaj leader and Gandhi's contemporary; Gandhi never described him as his political guru.

question: In which year did Gopal Krishna Gokhale found the Servants of India Society?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1905.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Servants of India Society was founded by Gokhale at Pune in 1905 to train selfless national workers (भारत सेवक समाज की स्थापना — गोखले, 1905)

 

• Its members took vows of poverty and lifelong service, and the society also worked to spread education and social reform among Indians.

 

• The society's aim was to prepare Indians who would devote their lives to the country by constitutional means rather than agitation.

 

• V. S. Srinivasa Sastri and N. M. Joshi were prominent members, and Joshi later became a labour leader.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The year 1905 also saw the Partition of Bengal and the Benares Congress where Gokhale presided.

 

• N. M. Joshi founded the Social Service League in Bombay in 1911.

 

• The Servants of India Society's headquarters was at Pune.

 

• Gokhale's disciples ran Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics established in 1930.

 

NOTE

 

• 1885 (Option 1): The year 1885 is the year the Indian National Congress was founded at Bombay under W. C. Bonnerjee, not the date of Gokhale's own society, which came two decades afterwards.

 

• 1916 (Option 2): In 1916 Tilak and Annie Besant launched their Home Rule Leagues and the Lucknow Pact was concluded; Gokhale had by then died, in 1915, so the society predates it.

 

• 1920 (Option 3): The year 1920 marks the Non-Cooperation Movement under Gandhi and Tilak's death; Gokhale had died five years earlier and his society was already fifteen years old.

question:
Consider the following statements about Gopal Krishna Gokhale:

1. He joined the Indian National Congress in 1889.

2. M. G. Ranade was his mentor.

3. He presided over the Calcutta session of the Congress in 1917.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Gokhale entered the Congress in 1889 and rose to be one of its leading Moderates (गोखले ने 1889 में कांग्रेस की सदस्यता ली)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Mahadev Govind Ranade, the Pune judge and reformer, was his political and intellectual guru and shaped his belief in gradual constitutional progress.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Calcutta session of 1917 was presided over by Annie Besant, the first woman president; Gokhale had died in 1915.

 

• Gokhale's actual presidency came at the Benares session of 1905, a point often tested alongside his death in 1915.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ranade founded the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha's reformist tradition and the Social Conference in 1887.

 

• Gokhale's essays in the Sudharak and his speeches in the Imperial Legislative Council earned him respect.

 

• Gandhi's tribute to Gokhale described him as the purest of men in public life.

 

• Gokhale got the Morley-Minto reform proposals discussed in the council.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): This option combines the true statement 2 with the false statement 3; Gokhale died in 1915 and so could not preside over the 1917 session that Annie Besant chaired.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Statement 1 is true but the answer wrongly drops statement 2 and keeps statement 3, which fails because Gokhale was not alive in 1917 when Besant presided at Calcutta.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): All three cannot hold because statement 3 is impossible: Gokhale passed away in February 1915, while the 1917 Calcutta session had Annie Besant as its first woman president.

question:
Assertion (A): Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.

Reason (R): The society aimed to train Indians to dedicate their lives to the country and to spread education among Indians.

Which one of the following is correct?
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: Gokhale established the Servants of India Society at Pune in 1905 (गोखले की भारत सेवक समाज — 1905)

 

• Reason R is true: the society recruited full-time workers who took a vow of poverty and service, and it also promoted education among the masses.

 

• R directly explains the purpose behind A, since the society was created precisely as a training body for selfless national workers.

 

• Its members were expected to work through constitutional means and avoid partisan or personal gain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The society later ran the English weekly Hitavada from Nagpur, spreading its ideas beyond Maharashtra.

 

• Membership was open only to those prepared to serve at a small allowance of about fifty rupees per month.

 

• Gokhale's friend Ranade shared the vision of a trained cadre of public workers.

 

• The society's work covered famine relief, women's education and the uplift of depressed classes.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): This is incorrect because R is not merely a side fact; the aim of training selfless workers and spreading education is the very reason the society was founded in 1905.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): Reason R is accurate, not false: the society was meant to train Indians for national service and education, which matches the objectives laid down by Gokhale in 1905.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 3): Assertion A is accurate, not false, since Gokhale did found the society in 1905 at Pune; the pairing with a false A therefore cannot stand.

question: Valentine Chirol, editor of The Times of London, described which Indian leader as the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was called the Father of Indian Unrest by Valentine Chirol in his book Indian Unrest (1910) (भारतीय अशांति के जनक — बाल गंगाधर तिलक)

 

• The British considered Tilak the chief inspirer of the aggressive nationalism that grew after the Partition of Bengal.

 

• Indian admirers gave him the title Lokmanya, meaning one honoured and accepted by the people.

 

• His Marathi paper Kesari and the English Mahratta carried his demand for Swaraj and prompted his prosecutions for sedition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak was sentenced to six years' imprisonment in 1908 and sent to Mandalay jail.

 

• Chirol's book Indian Unrest was a collection of Times articles on the unrest of 1907-08.

 

• Tilak's slogan was 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'.

 

• He died on 1 August 1920, the day Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai (Option 2): Lajpat Rai, the Lion of Punjab, was deported to Mandalay in 1907 after the agrarian unrest, but the Father of Indian Unrest label was reserved by Chirol for Tilak.

 

• Bipin Chandra Pal (Option 3): Bipin Chandra Pal was a fiery Swadeshi orator and part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio; Chirol did not apply this particular epithet to him.

 

• Aurobindo Ghosh (Option 4): Aurobindo Ghosh was a Swadeshi-era extremist who was later tried in the Alipore Bomb case; the Father of Indian Unrest title does not belong to him.

question: Kesari (in Marathi) and Mahratta (in English) were the newspapers published by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak started Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) in 1881 to awaken the people (केसरी और मराठा के संस्थापक — बाल गंगाधर तिलक)

 

• Through these papers he criticised British policies, supported famine-hit peasants and spread the call for Swaraj.

 

• His articles on the Bengal partition and on terrorism led to sedition charges and a six-year sentence in 1908.

 

• Gopal Ganesh Agarkar and Vishnushastri Chiplunkar were his early associates in the Deccan Education Society and the newspapers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Agarkar later left Kesari and started his own paper Sudharak.

 

• The Deccan Education Society was set up in 1884 and began Fergusson College in 1885.

 

• Tilak was charged in 1897 after the Pune plague, when Rand was assassinated by the Chapekar brothers.

 

• Kesari continued to be published from Pune well after Independence.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 1): Gokhale was associated with the Servants of India Society and other organs such as the Sudharak, but he was never the owner of the Marathi and English newspapers Kesari and Mahratta.

 

• Annie Besant (Option 2): Annie Besant ran Commonweal and the daily New India in the Home Rule period, which were her papers in English, not the Pune-based Kesari or Mahratta.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee (Option 3): Banerjee edited the Bengalee, a Calcutta English paper, and is not connected with the two Pune papers published by Tilak and his colleagues.

question: Tilak popularised the Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav as a public festival from which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1893.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tilak began the Sarvajanik (public) Ganeshotsav in Pune in 1893 to bring people of all castes together (सार्वजनिक गणेशोत्सव का आरंभ 1893)

 

• Public celebration, with speeches and processions, turned a household worship into a platform for national unity and political education.

 

• In 1895 he added Shiv Jayanti, linking nationalist sentiment with the memory of Shivaji.

 

• Today the Ganeshotsav is one of the largest festivals of Maharashtra.

 

• The festival also had a social purpose, because it replaced caste-bound household worship with a gathering open to people of every caste and community.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The government viewed the festivals warily and banned processions near mosques after communal tensions.

 

• Tilak was critical of the Age of Consent Bill of 1891 on grounds of foreign interference in religion.

 

• The Shivaji festival at Raigad was inaugurated in 1896.

 

• His earlier work in the Deccan Education Society dated from 1880 onward.

 

NOTE

 

• 1857 (Option 1): The year 1857 saw the Revolt against the Company; Tilak was then a one-year-old child, born in 1856, and the festival was started decades later.

 

• 1905 (Option 2): In 1905 the Bengal partition triggered Swadeshi agitation and Tilak backed boycott; the Ganeshotsav as a public festival had already been in place for twelve years by then.

 

• 1916 (Option 4): The year 1916 is when Tilak launched the Home Rule League and signed the Lucknow Pact, which is a political landmark rather than the festival's starting point.

question:
Consider the following statements about Bal Gangadhar Tilak:

1. He wrote 'Arctic Home of the Vedas', suggesting the Arctic as the original home of the Aryans.

2. He wrote 'Gita Rahasya' while imprisoned.

3. He started the Arya Gazette.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Tilak's Arctic Home of the Vedas (1903) argued, using Vedic astronomical evidence, that the Aryans originated in the Arctic region (आर्कटिक होम इन द वेदाज — तिलक की रचना)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the Gita Rahasya, a commentary on the Bhagavad Gita stressing karma yoga, was composed during his six-year term at Mandalay jail.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the Arya Gazette was founded by Lala Lajpat Rai, not Tilak; Tilak's papers were Kesari and Mahratta.

 

• The Gita Rahasya was published in 1915 after his release and became widely read in Marathi and Hindi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak also wrote The Orion (1893), on the antiquity of the Vedas.

 

• He gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' at Belgaum in 1916.

 

• Lajpat Rai's Arya Gazette was an Urdu and Hindi weekly from Lahore.

 

• Mandalay is in Burma, where Tilak was held from 1908 to 1914.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Statement 3 is wrong because the Arya Gazette was Lajpat Rai's paper from Lahore, and this option also leaves out the true claim about the Arctic Home of the Vedas.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): The combination drops statement 2 and includes statement 3; Gita Rahasya was indeed written in jail, while the Arya Gazette is associated with Lajpat Rai.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): The full set is not correct as statement 3 misattributes the Arya Gazette to Tilak, who instead edited Kesari and Mahratta.

question:
Assertion (A): Bal Gangadhar Tilak is popularly known as 'Lokmanya'.

Reason (R): The people honoured him with this title for his leadership and service to the nation.

Which one of the following is correct?
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: Tilak is remembered as Lokmanya, a title meaning 'respected by the people' (लोकमान्य — लोगों द्वारा सम्मानित)

 

• Reason R is true: the title was a popular honour bestowed by the people rather than conferred by any authority, in recognition of his Swaraj slogan and sacrifices.

 

• Hence R explains A fully: the epithet arose out of public recognition of his leadership.

 

• The British, by contrast, labelled him the Father of Indian Unrest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak was tried for sedition in 1897 and 1908, and Jinnah defended him in the 1908 trial.

 

• Tilak never held the office of Congress president, though his influence shaped several sessions.

 

• Annie Besant's Home Rule League and his own were launched in 1916.

 

• He founded the Deccan Education Society with Agarkar and Chiplunkar.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): The relationship is more than coincidence, since the reason itself describes how the title arose; calling R a mere extra fact would ignore that Lokmanya was a popular honour.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): Reason R is not false, because the title was indeed given by the people in appreciation of his services, which is why it carries the sense of public honour.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): Assertion A cannot be called false, because Lokmanya is one of the best-known epithets in Indian history and is attached to Tilak in every standard account.

question: All of the following are associated with Bal Gangadhar Tilak EXCEPT:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Servants of India Society.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Servants of India Society was founded in 1905 by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, and is therefore not associated with Tilak (भारत सेवक समाज — गोखले की संस्था, तिलक की नहीं)

 

• Kesari was Tilak's Marathi newspaper and Mahratta his English weekly, both published from Pune.

 

• The Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav was turned into a public festival by Tilak in 1893, with Shiv Jayanti following in 1895.

 

• Tilak and Gokhale represented the Extremist and Moderate wings respectively, which makes the confusion between their institutions a favourite exam trap.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak's school-based institution was the Deccan Education Society.

 

• Gokhale's society expected members to avoid agitation politics.

 

• The Surat split of 1907 pitted Tilak's camp against Gokhale's.

 

• Tilak died in 1920 and Gokhale in 1915.

 

• Another institution Tilak helped found was the New English School at Pune in 1880, a model of nationalist education later tied to the Deccan Education Society.

 

NOTE

 

• Kesari (Option 1): Kesari was Tilak's own Marathi newspaper, started in 1881 and edited by him, so it is plainly linked to him and cannot be the odd one out in this list.

 

• Mahratta (Option 3): Mahratta was the English-language weekly he ran alongside Kesari to reach a wider audience, which makes it one of the items that do belong with Tilak.

 

• Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav (Option 4): The public Ganeshotsav from 1893 is among Tilak's best-known cultural initiatives, used for building nationalist feeling, so it is not the exception here.

question: Which leader is known as 'Punjab Kesari' or the 'Lion of Punjab'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lala Lajpat Rai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai was called Punjab Kesari for his courage and leadership in the politics of the Punjab (पंजाब केसरी — लाला लाजपत राय)

 

• Born in 1865 and trained as a lawyer, he was a leader of the Arya Samaj and the Extremist wing of the Congress.

 

• He co-founded the Punjab National Bank in 1894 and started the paper Arya Gazette.

 

• He was part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio together with Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• He was injured in a lathi-charge during a protest against the Simon Commission at Lahore in 1928 and died shortly afterwards.

 

• He presided over the Calcutta Special Session of 1920.

 

• He founded the Servants of the People Society in 1921.

 

• Bhagat Singh and his comrades sought revenge for his death by killing Saunders.

 

NOTE

 

• Bipin Chandra Pal (Option 1): Bipin Chandra Pal came from Bengal and is remembered as a Swadeshi orator and journalist; the Punjab Kesari title belongs to Lajpat Rai, his partner in the Lal-Bal-Pal triad.

 

• Sardar Bhagat Singh (Option 2): Bhagat Singh is remembered as Shaheed-e-Azam after his hanging in 1931; he was not known by the Punjab Kesari title that belongs to the older leader Lajpat Rai.

 

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Option 4): Abdul Ghaffar Khan was the Frontier Gandhi and Badshah Khan from the North-West Frontier Province, a region and title quite different from the Punjab Kesari epithet.

question:
Consider the following statements about Lala Lajpat Rai:

1. He co-founded the Punjab National Bank in 1894.

2. He founded the newspaper Arya Gazette.

3. He wrote the Gita Rahasya.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Lajpat Rai was among the founders of the Punjab National Bank, established at Lahore in 1894 as a swadeshi bank (पंजाब नेशनल बैंक के सह-संस्थापक — लाला लाजपत राय)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he started the Arya Gazette, reflecting his close association with the Arya Samaj and the DAV educational movement.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Gita Rahasya was written by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Mandalay jail; Lajpat Rai's well-known books include Unhappy India and The Story of My Deportation.

 

• Lajpat Rai's life thus mixes banking, journalism and politics, which explains his wide appeal in the Punjab.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unhappy India (1928) was his answer to Katherine Mayo's Mother India.

 

• He was deported to Mandalay in 1907 after the Punjab agrarian agitation but released within months.

 

• He wrote Young India in 1916, which is different from Gandhi's weekly of the same name.

 

• The Punjab National Bank's first office opened at Anarkali, Lahore, in 1895.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): This choice includes statement 3, which is false because the Gita Rahasya is Tilak's work, and it fails to include statement 1 about the Punjab National Bank that Lajpat Rai really did co-found.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Statement 3 credits Lajpat Rai with a Tilak composition, and the option also omits his Arya Gazette, which is a genuine journalistic venture of his.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Adding statement 3 makes the set wrong, because the commentary on the Gita written in prison was by Tilak and not by the Punjab leader.

question: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Home Rule League of America in 1917 at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is New York.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai established the Home Rule League of America in New York in 1917 to rally American opinion for Indian self-government (1917 में न्यूयॉर्क में होम रूल लीग ऑफ अमेरिका — लाला लाजपत राय)

 

• He had gone abroad in 1914 and, stranded by the First World War, spent several years in the United States working for India's cause.

 

• In America he also edited the journal Young India and wrote the book Young India (1916), which criticised British rule.

 

• The effort paralleled the Home Rule Leagues of Tilak and Annie Besant in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• His stay in the United States lasted until 1919, and he used it to lobby American public opinion against British policy.

 

• The Ghadar movement was concentrated on the Pacific coast, particularly San Francisco.

 

• He returned to India in 1920 and presided over the Calcutta Special Session.

 

• India House, a hub for revolutionaries, was based in London.

 

NOTE

 

• London (Option 1): London was the base of Shyamji Krishna Varma's India House and the Indian Home Rule Society; Lajpat Rai's 1917 league was set up in the United States, not Britain.

 

• Chicago (Option 2): Chicago was not the seat of Lajpat Rai's organisation, although he travelled in the Midwest; the Home Rule League of America was set up on the East Coast.

 

• San Francisco (Option 3): San Francisco was the centre of the Ghadar Party, founded by Punjabi migrants in 1913, and not where Lajpat Rai put up his Home Rule League of America.

question: Bipin Chandra Pal, who began as a moderate and later turned extremist, played an important role in which movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swadeshi Movement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bipin Chandra Pal played an important role in the Swadeshi Movement (1905-08) that followed the Partition of Bengal (बिपिन चंद्र पाल — स्वदेशी आंदोलन के प्रमुख नेता)

 

• He preached nationalism across India through powerful speeches and writings, and was one of the Lal-Bal-Pal triad of Extremists.

 

• His journals such as New India (English weekly) and Vande Mataram made him a prominent voice of the Bengal nationalists.

 

• He later parted ways with Gandhi over the methods of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pal advocated a federation of free states within an Indian Commonwealth in his later writings.

 

• He was a Brahmo Samaj follower from Sylhet.

 

• The Swadeshi Movement used boycott of British goods and national education.

 

• Aurobindo Ghosh was Pal's close associate in the Bengal extremist camp.

 

• The Lal-Bal-Pal trio of Lajpat Rai, Tilak and Pal pushed the Congress towards boycott and national education between 1905 and 1908.

 

NOTE

 

• Non-Cooperation Movement (Option 1): The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920 under Gandhi; Pal criticised its methods and was no longer a leading figure by then, so it was not his major campaign.

 

• Champaran Satyagraha (Option 2): The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was Gandhi's first Indian satyagraha for indigo cultivators in Bihar, a peasant struggle in which Pal had no part.

 

• Quit India Movement (Option 4): The Quit India Movement of 1942 came a decade after Pal's death in 1932, and he could not have taken part in that final mass struggle.

question: After leaving active politics, Aurobindo Ghosh, an extremist leader of the Swadeshi Movement, settled at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pondicherry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aurobindo Ghosh retired to Pondicherry in 1910 and devoted himself to spiritual practice and the philosophy of integral yoga (पुदुचेरी में श्री अरविंद आश्रम)

 

• Earlier he was a leader of the Bengal extremists in the Swadeshi Movement and was tried in the Alipore Conspiracy Case of 1908, though acquitted.

 

• His ashram, set up with the Mother (Mirra Alfassa), later became the base of the Auroville community.

 

• Pondicherry then lay in French territory, which allowed him to escape British surveillance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• He edited the English daily Bande Mataram during the Swadeshi days.

 

• His major works include The Life Divine and Savitri.

 

• He gave up politics after being acquitted in 1909.

 

• Pondicherry became part of India in 1954.

 

• Aurobindo's brother Barindra Kumar Ghose led the Anushilan-linked Maniktala group, which was tried with him in the 1908 Alipore Bomb Case.

 

NOTE

 

• Benares (Option 1): Benares is the seat of the Hindu University and Annie Besant's Central Hindu College, but Aurobindo did not settle there; his ashram was in the French territory of Pondicherry.

 

• Santiniketan (Option 3): Santiniketan is the Bengal village where Tagore established Visva-Bharati; Aurobindo moved further south, to the French enclave on the Coromandel coast.

 

• Wardha (Option 4): Wardha in Maharashtra was associated with Gandhi's Sevagram ashram in the 1930s and was not the retreat chosen by Aurobindo after his political career.

question: Who became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annie Besant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Annie Besant was elected the first woman President of the Congress at the Calcutta session of 1917 (कांग्रेस की प्रथम महिला अध्यक्ष — एनी बेसेंट)

 

• She had joined the Congress and launched the All India Home Rule League in 1916, which put self-government at the centre of national politics.

 

• She edited the papers Commonweal and New India and stayed in the Theosophical Society until her death in 1933.

 

• Her election followed her internment by the Madras government in 1917, which provoked nationwide protest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman president at Kanpur in 1925.

 

• Nellie Sengupta, a British-born woman, presided over the Calcutta session of 1933.

 

• Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister, of Uttar Pradesh, in 1963.

 

• Besant arrived in India in 1893.

 

• Besant's Central Hindu College at Benares, founded in 1898, was later merged into the Banaras Hindu University that Madan Mohan Malaviya established in 1916.

 

NOTE

 

• Sarojini Naidu (Option 2): Sarojini Naidu presided over the Kanpur session of 1925 as the first Indian woman President; Besant's election came eight years earlier, in 1917.

 

• Nellie Sengupta (Option 3): Nellie Sengupta became president at Calcutta in 1933, long after Besant, and was British by birth; she was the third woman to lead the Congress.

 

• Sucheta Kripalani (Option 4): Sucheta Kripalani became prominent in the Quit India days and later was Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, but she never presided over a Congress session in 1917.

question:
Consider the following statements about Annie Besant:

1. She arrived in India in 1893 as a member of the Theosophical Society.

2. She launched the All India Home Rule League in 1916.

3. She was the first Indian woman to become President of the Congress.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Besant came to India in 1893 as a member of the Theosophical Society and settled at Adyar, Madras (1893 में भारत आगमन — एनी बेसेंट)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: in 1916 she launched the Home Rule League, with headquarters at Adyar, and campaigned for self-government through the newspapers New India and Commonweal.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: she was the first woman President of the Congress (1917), but she was not Indian by birth; Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President in 1925.

 

• She also fought social evils such as caste discrimination and child marriage and worked to improve education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• She founded the Central Hindu College at Benares in 1898, which grew into Banaras Hindu University.

 

• Her Home Rule League was launched in September 1916, months after Tilak's league in April.

 

• She was interned in June 1917 by Governor Lord Pentland.

 

• She died at Adyar in 1933 at the age of 85.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): This version wrongly includes statement 3 and drops statement 1; Besant was the first woman president but not an Indian woman, since she was born in London.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): The pair leaves out statement 2 on the Home Rule League of 1916 and keeps statement 3, which mislabels Besant as Indian, whereas Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman president.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): All three cannot be right because statement 3 states that she was Indian, while she was a British-born theosophist who took up the Indian cause.
